summary: Attacked the Function fields area — DrinfeldModulesAndTModules, FunctionFieldArithmetic and GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands: 3 roadmaps, 25 stages, 24 accepted paper routes, the best route-to-stage ratio of any area I have taken. One finding, medium: the Anderson-Brownawell-Papanikolas linear independence criterion is named by no layer, while DM.8 assumes 'the exact linear-independence hypothesis' as an input and three routed papers rely on the criterion there, one of them saying outright that the layer does not state it. Everything else is clean, and the dependency bookkeeping is the most exact I have seen: both roadmaps with an empty consumers list are genuine sinks, and the third declares precisely the three consumers it has, no more and no fewer.
checked: All 25 stages of the three roadmaps — DrinfeldModulesAndTModules 9, FunctionFieldArithmetic 8, GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands 8 — with their inputs, construction clauses, acceptance clauses and source routes, and the accepted audit verdict for each: 21 not built, 4 partly built.
Eligibility, measured rather than assumed: none of the papers this session has reviewed routes into this area, checked at route granularity across all 207 paper result files.

All 24 route reasons in full. The distribution: GlobalShtukas 10 (GS.0 5, GS.1 5, GS.2 3), DrinfeldModules 9 (DM.8 4, DM.0 3), FunctionFieldArithmetic 5 (FA.6 3). 24 routes across 25 stages is the densest coverage of any area I have red-teamed, so the omissions head had real material to work with, unlike part 3 of the arithmetic-geometry area where 4 routes covered 111 stages.

Dependency bookkeeping, which is exact here and worth recording precisely because the roadmap I filed a high-severity finding against in RT-AREA-arithmeticgeometry-3 fails the same test. Both roadmaps with `consumers: []` are genuine sinks: DrinfeldModulesAndTModules is cited by exactly two roadmaps, SchemeAndStackFoundations and FunctionFieldArithmetic, which are exactly its two declared prerequisites citing it as their consumer; GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands is cited by exactly four, which are exactly its four declared prerequisites. FunctionFieldArithmetic is cited by seven — its four prerequisites plus DrinfeldModulesAndTModules, GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands and ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction — and it declares `consumers: ['DrinfeldModulesAndTModules', 'ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction', 'GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands']`, which is that set exactly. For all three roadmaps the cross-roadmap stage `requires` edges are contained in the declared prerequisites.

The opaque-handle check that produced the high-severity finding in part 3 of the arithmetic-geometry area, applied here as a generalisable test: no roadmap in this area references another by a bare pull-request number of the form #NN, so every cross-roadmap reference is resolvable to a roadmap id.

A systematic scan of all 24 route reasons for routes that record their own unmet need — UNACCEPTED, 'does not name/own/supply/assign/cover', 'no owner', 'ownership decision', 'needs a separate', 'not supplied by', 'no layer', 'absent from'. It returned nothing, and that was a false clean of my own making: the finding below is stated in a route as 'the layer does not state the criterion itself', and my pattern did not include 'state'. Reading the reasons caught what the scan missed, which is the method note worth carrying — the signal phrase varies, so the scan narrows the reading rather than replacing it.

The remaining hot stages read against their route reasons, for objects a routed paper needs that the target stage does not name. GS.0 (global Bun_G with level structures, Harder-Narasimhan bounded opens, adelic rational points), GS.1 (global Hecke stacks and modifications, geometric Satake), GS.2 and FA.6 (automorphic forms over a function field with cuspidal spaces, Hecke correspondences and the unramified Satake dictionary) all name what their routes send them, and several routes say so explicitly — SHENDE-TSIMERMAN-17 calls its PGL_2 correspondence 'an acceptance instance, not a second moduli owner', CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26 supplies refinements 'not a second automorphic foundation', YU-23 says 'do not duplicate the upstream curve/function-field dictionary'.

PAPER-LAFFORGUE-18's route, which is the strongest evidence that the GlobalShtukas roadmap is correctly scoped rather than merely plausible: the paper is the roadmap's own named source stage by stage, and the route quotes the source routes back — GS.0's reads 'V. Lafforgue global bundle/level setup', GS.1's 'V. Lafforgue geometric Satake input', GS.2's 'V. Lafforgue shtuka construction', GS.3's 'V. Lafforgue Hecke-finite cohomology construction', GS.4's 'V. Lafforgue Drinfeld-lemma'. A roadmap whose eight stages each name the right part of the one paper that proves the theorem is not planning blind.

PAPER-FENG-24's route, recorded because a red team should notice when a source adds nothing: 'Sections 2 and 5.1 are a careful, self-contained account of exactly what these layers plan, and the paper is a good source for them even though everything it says there is already planned.' That is the opposite of an omission and confirms GS.1 to GS.5's coverage from an independent direction.

The library boundary, which can yield little here and for the same reason as parts 1 and 2 of the arithmetic-geometry area: 21 of 25 stages are audited `not built`, including all eight of GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands. The four partly-built stages are one in DrinfeldModulesAndTModules and three in FunctionFieldArithmetic, the foundational end. No stage instructs construction of something an audit records as built.

Library trees, with sizes printed beside every result after two wrong paths produced false cleans earlier in this session: a full Mathlib checkout of 8556 .lean files and the Tau Ceti library tree of 5268.

findings.where: DrinfeldModulesAndTModules:DM.8 (Periods, logarithms and algebraic independence), and the atlas as a whole
findings.claim: The Anderson-Brownawell-Papanikolas linear independence criterion has no owner. DM.8's construction clause tells a worker to 'deduce algebraic independence from the exact linear-independence hypothesis by calculating the Galois group', so it takes that hypothesis as an input, and the ABP criterion is the theorem that supplies it — but no layer in either roadmap directory states the criterion, and DM.8's source route names only Papanikolas. Three of the nine routes into this roadmap rely on it at DM.8, and one of them says in so many words that the layer does not state it. So the stage's central deduction rests on a theorem that nothing in the atlas plans.
findings.evidence: DM.8's construction clause, in full on this point: 'For Carlitz logarithms of algebraic arguments, deduce algebraic independence from the exact linear-independence hypothesis by calculating the Galois group.' Its source route names one paper: 'Papanikolas arXiv:math/0506078, Tannakian/difference-group and Carlitz-logarithm theorems.' The three routes that rely on the criterion. PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24, which states the gap: 'DM.8 plans the Tannakian difference-Galois theory of rigid analytically trivial t-motives after Papanikolas, which is built on the Anderson-Brownawell-Papanikolas linear independence criterion; the layer does not state the criterion itself. This paper uses it in the form quoted as its Theorem 2.2'. PAPER-WEI-26, routing to DM.0, DM.2, DM.4 and DM.8: '80 is the actual ABP lifting criterion (DM.8)'. PAPER-NGODAC-21, routing to DM.8: 'Generic coefficient twists, Tate/entire analytic interfaces, denominator descent and ABP lifting support period/logarithm theory and every higher-depth consumer.' Ownership searches across research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/ and research/blueprint/roadmaps/: 'Anderson-Brownawell-Papanikolas' returns 0 files, 'ABP' as a whole word returns 0, and 'linear independence criterion' returns 0. 'Papanikolas' returns exactly one file, DrinfeldModulesAndTModules itself, which is DM.8's source-route citation of the Tannakian paper and not the criterion.
findings.fix: Name the criterion as a target, either as its own stage before DM.8 or as an explicit input of DM.8 rather than an assumed hypothesis: the Anderson-Brownawell-Papanikolas linear independence criterion in the form the routed papers use, which PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24 quotes as its Theorem 2.2 and PAPER-WEI-26 calls the ABP lifting criterion. DM.8's source route should cite it alongside Papanikolas, since the Tannakian paper it currently names builds on the criterion rather than proving it. The three routed papers are the sources, and PAPER-NGODAC-21's route already asks for ABP lifting to sit in this shared owner rather than being re-planned in a Part II ('do not re-plan these inside Part II'), so the owner should be here. Once stated, DM.8's phrase 'the exact linear-independence hypothesis' can cite the criterion instead of leaving the worker to supply it.
